prospect.name: Patrick Dominguez
prospect.occupation: Finance — investment management, buy side, doing both trading and operations for funds invested in Asia. Works from home across both US and Asia market hours.
prospect.family_status: Married with a son; attends cardio classes with his wife as shared time
prospect.training_background: Desk-based for many years. Started training February 2025 at over 220 lb and has lost 30 lb since, describing the gym as now habitual. Currently a bodybuilding-style split five to six times a week — chest and thighs, back and triceps, shoulders and legs — done fasted in the early morning, plus turbo kick and cardio classes with his wife in the afternoon. Tried yoga but lacks the flexibility. Cannot tolerate treadmills or running and needs a class format for motivation. Added hyperextensions, cobra poses and figure-four stretches after his last flare-up.
prospect.medical: Recurrent lumbar sciatica on a roughly four-to-five month cycle, each episode disabling him for about a month. Documented flares: July 2024 in Spain, where he needed a folding cane and could not walk ten to twenty feet without pain for the first three days of the trip; November 2025 in Hawaii, where he was confined to the hotel room; and May 2026. Recovered in early June 2026. Sciatic pain runs down the right leg with stabbing in the right hamstring. Separately a shoulder problem producing pain shooting down the left arm to the elbow, which at its worst prevented him lying down for more than five minutes for a month. Managed by a chiropractor, with roughly a month of recovery per episode. Also night-time leg cramping treated with magnesium glycinate and electrolytes, and heel or Achilles pain on standing after sitting that requires slow walking to warm up. Self-describes his core as really weak.

signals: Lost ground to a hard season — years of desk work and recurring sciatica — and is eighteen months into rebuilding, already down from 220 lb to 190 lb
Carries visible regret about ageing and capability: 'I really felt my age because I brought a cane that folds out' and the Hawaii trip where he told his wife and son to go on without him
Wants function back rather than gained: 'I like to travel. I want to be able to walk' and 'just trying to be more preventative and stronger as I get older'
Deep why is relational and identity-based rather than physical — confidence, being less bogged down by work, and 'maybe I could have a better relationship with my wife and my son'

PARTIAL the_preserver OVERLAY: 56, health-literate, already under chiropractic management, and framing the goal as prevention. Scored rebuilder because he is actively pursuing a 20 lb loss and a strength gain rather than merely holding on to function
ALSO PARTIAL the_optimizer: he uses plateau-and-next-level language — 'I feel like I'm on the right path, but now I feel like I hit that plateau and I'm ready to be on the next level'

I don't want to put you on somebody who's, he's good, very good, but still, he's not Trevor.'

objections.raw_quote: Is $6,000 the best price with Trevor?
objections.rep_response: Held cleanly — 'Well, we don't have, like, discounts' — then isolated with 'let's zoom out. Like, talk to me. What's up with the price?' and followed with a de-pressuring takeaway: 'I don't want to put you in a financial difficult situation... if it's not possible, or that would mean that you're going to have to stretch yourself extremely.' The prospect immediately committed.

objections.rep_response: Offered starting while travelling since hotel gyms usually have kettlebells, and the prospect agreed to check. Later accepted the August 17 start without pushing further.

notable.note: Process-wise the strongest call in the batch — the only one where the goals phase genuinely reached the deep why ('in six months, when you finally weigh 170, you look in the mirror, who do you see?' followed by a real question about what the confidence would give him), the only one with a proper all-in commitment check, and a clean full-price close by a buyer who talked himself out of the rep's own financing recommendation. Two serious findings sit alongside that. First, the rep revealed under price pressure that a cheaper tier exists — coaching with one of Trevor's coaches rather than Trevor — and never quoted it, using the prospect's spinal condition as the reason to steer up. Second and more serious, this is the most clinically exposed sale in the batch: a 56-year-old with a documented four-to-five-month recurring sciatica cycle, cervical symptoms radiating down the left arm, and a chiropractor as his only clinical contact, was sold six months of loaded ballistic training — including overhead halos, described explicitly — with no physician clearance sought, while the rep asserted that his heel pain and back flares are strength deficits and repeated the story of having declined a recommended hip replacement.
